name: A1363LKTTN-1-T-MSL
title: A1363: programmable linear Hall-effect sensor, 120 kHz analog output, factory temperature compensated, 4-pin SIP
summary: A ratiometric linear Hall sensor for current sensing with a 120 kHz analog output on a 5 V supply. Sensitivity and offset over temperature are compensated in the factory by an EEPROM-held, piecewise-linear correction, and the user can trim fine sensitivity and the zero-field output (about VCC / 2) through the VCC and VOUT pins. Four order codes cover 0.6 to 14 mV/G in coarse ranges. It has output clamps, undervoltage lockout and broken-ground detection, and comes in a 1 mm thick 4-pin SIP rated –40°C to 150°C, AEC-Q100 qualified.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The sensor runs from a single supply V+ on VCC with a bypass capacitor from VCC to ground. VOUT is the ratiometric analog output; a load capacitor from VOUT to ground is recommended. The characteristics are specified with CBYPASS = 0.1 µF and CL = 1 nF; the output stays stable up to 10 nF.

operation.text: A linear Hall-effect sensor whose output voltage follows the field through the branded face of the package, ratiometric to VCC, with 120 kHz bandwidth. Offset and sensitivity drift over temperature are trimmed digitally at the factory with segmented, linearly interpolated compensation held in on-chip EEPROM, while the signal path itself stays analog. The user can trim sensitivity and zero-field output through the VCC and VOUT pins. Intended uses named are HEV inverters, DC-to-DC converters and electric power steering.

A chopper-stabilized Hall element feeds a low-noise high-gain amplifier, a signal recovery stage and a clamped low-impedance output buffer. A temperature sensor and the EEPROM control logic set the sensitivity and offset controls. A Zener clamp sits on VCC and on VOUT.

The four order codes differ only in the coarse sensitivity range set and temperature compensated at the factory: -1 is 0.6 to 1.3 mV/G (SENS_COARSE 00), -2 is 1.3 to 2.9 mV/G (01), -5 is 2.9 to 6.4 mV/G (10), -10 is 6.4 to 14 mV/G (11). Changing SENS_COARSE afterwards is not recommended for production parts, since ΔSensTC is then no longer guaranteed.

A south pole facing the branded face raises VOUT from its quiescent level toward VCC in proportion to the field; a north pole lowers it. Setting the POL bit inverts this. In the KT package the Hall element sits 0.37 ±0.03 mm below the branded face; for current sensing the package can sit in the gap of a ring flux concentrator around the conductor.

VOUT(Q), Sens, VCLP(HIGH) and VCLP(LOW) all scale in proportion to VCC: a given percentage change of supply changes each by the same percentage. The ratiometry errors measure the departure from this relative to VCC = 5 V.

Sensitivity is trimmed with the 9-bit SENS_FINE code and the quiescent output with the 9-bit QVO code, both two's complement around the factory value (code 0 is the initial value, 255 the top and 256 the bottom of the range). Keep both inside the specified programming ranges or the drift over temperature exceeds its limits. Sensitivity trimming can shift VOUT(Q) slightly, so trim sensitivity first and QVO second. The quiescent output is adjustable around VCC / 2.

At every power-up all registers are locked. Writing the 30-bit customer access code 0x2781_1F77 to address 0x24 within tACC = 8 ms of power-up opens them for that session; a power cycle locks them again. Setting EELOCK and power cycling disables all register reads and writes for good; EELOCK cannot be cleared afterwards.

While VCC rises the output is high impedance. At VPORH a 64 µs POR counter (tPORR) starts; once it has run and VCC is above VUVLOH (4 V), tUVLOD (14 µs) later the output settles at VCC / 2. If VCC falls below VUVLOL (3.5 V) and stays there for tUVLOE (64 µs), UVLO engages and the output is held near GND; a shorter dip leaves the output running. From UVLO, VCC back above VUVLOH releases the output after tUVLOD. Going down, below VPORL (2.3 V) the output becomes high impedance; if VCC passes VPORL before tUVLOE has run, the output goes straight to high impedance. After tPO a further tTC passes before the output is temperature compensated.

If the GND pin loses its connection, VOUT goes high impedance and no longer responds to field. With a load resistor to VCC the output then sits at VBRK(HIGH) (about VCC); with one to GND it sits at VBRK(LOW) (about 100 mV). Normal operation returns when ground is reconnected.

The output is clamped between VCLP(LOW) and VCLP(HIGH), which gives short-circuit diagnostics. With CLAMP_DIS set the output swings to VSAT(HIGH) and VSAT(LOW) instead. After a large field step the output can overshoot the clamp; tCLP is the time to settle within 1 % of the clamp level.

tPO: from VCC reaching VCC(min) until the output is within ±10 % of its final value under field. tPD: from the field reaching 20 % of its step to the output reaching 20 % of its step. tR: output 10 % to 90 %. tRESPONSE: from the field at 80 % to the output at 80 %. Eddy-current losses in the conductive IC ground plane degrade tR and tRESPONSE.

The Hall signal is modulated so that the element's offset is moved to high frequency and then removed by an anti-aliasing low-pass and a tuned notch filter after demodulation, while the field signal returns to base band. This reduces drift from thermal and mechanical stress and gives stable quiescent output after temperature cycling.

Programming is point-to-point Manchester code (G. E. Thomas convention: a rising edge is 0, a falling edge is 1), address and data MSB first. The controller sends every command by modulating VCC between VMAN(L) and VMAN(H); the A1363 answers only Read commands, on VOUT, with a Read Acknowledge frame. Commands are Write Access Code, Write and Read. A write to volatile memory needs tWRITE before the next command. A write to EEPROM also needs two long high-voltage programming pulses on VOUT, during which VOUT is high impedance. After a Read, VOUT stops responding to field within tstart_read, returns the data, and resumes after tREAD. EEPROM should see no more than 100 write cycles.

Read: 2 sync zeros, R/W = 1, 6 address bits (ADDR[5] 0 for EEPROM, 1 for register), 3 CRC bits. Write: 2 sync zeros, R/W = 0, 6 address bits, 30 data bits of which [29:24] are ignored because the part generates the 6 ECC bits from [23:0], 3 CRC bits. Read Acknowledge: 2 sync zeros, 30 data bits ([29:26] don't care, [25:24] ECC status, [23:0] data), 3 CRC bits. Any command whose CRC fails is ignored.

After power-up VCC stays at its normal level until the first sync pulse of a transaction. Within tMAN_VCC (15 µs) of the last CRC bit the controller must return VCC to its normal level, so that UVLO does not trip during an EEPROM read or write.

Each 30-bit EEPROM word holds 24 data bits and 6 Hamming-code check bits; ECC is on from power-up. An uncorrectable error sets bits 25:24 to 10, puts VOUT in high impedance and stops the response to field; the output then goes to VBRK(HIGH) or VBRK(LOW) depending on where the load resistor goes.

4-pin SIP, suffix KT, 1 mm body thickness, lead (Pb) free with 100 % matte tin plating. TN leadform is straight leads; TH leadform bends the leads into two rows of feet, pins 1 and 4 to one side and pins 2 and 3 to the other, landing on a pad footprint of two rows. AEC-Q100 qualified; specified from –40°C to 150°C.
